A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TetraJet research. All 15 pages of each version, including Appendices A-C, equations, figures and tables, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet1K pretraining results for DeiT and Swin, oscillation measurements, and ablation and hyperparameter studies in the main text and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original pretraining, oscillation, ablation and hyperparameter results, including the accuracy comparisons in Table 2 and supplementary experiments in Appendices B-C.

M1.justification: Truncation-free scaling, double quantization, stochastic backward rounding, Q-EMA and Q-Ramping are unchanged, including Algorithms 1-2. The corrected output symbol in Equation (1) does not change the described procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet1K classification through DeiT-Tiny/Small/Base and Swin-Tiny/Small pretraining. No datasets, tasks, domains or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains full-precision training, INT4 and Microscaling as comparators. Dampen and Freeze remain in Table 4, and Dampen remains in Table 3 and Figure 6. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported 90-epoch training recipes, model configurations, quantized layers, validation metrics and ablation settings are unchanged. Removing the optional matrix-confidence definition does not change the reported confidence-distribution evaluations.

E4.justification: The six-quantizer impact study, oscillation and stability analyses, quantization-strategy and FP4-format ablations, and hyperparameter sensitivity studies are retained unchanged in Table 1, Figures 2-6 and Appendices B-C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The same point estimates and training trajectories are presented.

E6.justification: Tables 1-10 and the plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains DeiT-B top-1 accuracies of 74.91% for TetraJet and 77.32% for TetraJet + Q-EMA. Appendix ablation and hyperparameter results also match.

T1.justification: v2 removes the optional definition of matrix-level quantization confidence as the mean of element-wise confidence values from Section 4.2 and Appendix A.2. The element-wise definitions and Section 3.4 gradient-unbiasedness derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about accurate MXFP4 training and oscillation reduction, including reducing accuracy degradation by more than 50% relative to the baseline.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting threshold crossings to instability and interpreting Q-EMA/Q-Ramping are unchanged. Appendix A retains the comparison with flipping frequency, and Appendix C.4 retains the qualification against simply combining the two methods.

D1.justification: Appendix C's pseudocode and hyperparameters, Appendix A's measurement intervals, and the code and training-recipe access information are unchanged. The new support acknowledgments provide no additional implementation or hardware specifications.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. COAT, Jetfire, DeiT and the bfloat16 reference receive publication or bibliographic metadata updates rather than becoming new citations or changing the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 corrects Equation (1)'s output symbol from X_i to P_i, regularizes quantizer notation, revises Appendix A headings, and adds acknowledgments and publication/affiliation information. The main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The first-page abstract/introduction placement and some paragraph spacing and page breaks change, with further reflow from acknowledgments and expanded references. The same six figures, ten tables and two algorithm displays remain without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (1) removes an inconsistency between the original value X_i and its FP4 representation P_i, while clearer quantizer notation modestly improves technical readability. The removed matrix-average definition was ancillary to the retained element-wise distribution analyses. The methodological and empirical support remains unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
